events.title: Trajan becomes Roman Emperor
events.description: On the death of Nerva, his adopted son Trajan, the first emperor born outside Italy, succeeded to the throne. His conquests of Dacia and Mesopotamia brought the empire to its greatest extent.
events.html: On the death of Nerva, his adopted son Trajan, the first emperor born outside Italy, succeeded to the throne. His conquests of Dacia and Mesopotamia brought the empire to its greatest extent.

events.title: Dante Alighieri is sentenced to exile from Florence
events.description: Florence's victorious Black Guelphs convicted Dante of corruption in his absence. He never returned home, and wrote the 'Divine Comedy' during his exile.
events.html: Florence's victorious Black Guelphs convicted Dante of corruption in his absence. He never returned home, and wrote the 'Divine Comedy' during his exile.

events.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born in Salzburg
events.description: The son of the court musician Leopold Mozart, he toured Europe as a child prodigy. In a life of 35 years he wrote more than 600 works, including 'The Marriage of Figaro' and 'Don Giovanni'.
events.html: The son of the court musician Leopold Mozart, he toured Europe as a child prodigy. In a life of 35 years he wrote more than 600 works, including 'The Marriage of Figaro' and 'Don Giovanni'.

events.title: Thomas Edison patents his incandescent lamp
events.description: Edison received US patent 223,898 for a carbon-filament lamp. Others had made electric bulbs, but his long-lasting design and supply system made electric lighting practical.
events.html: Edison received US patent 223,898 for a carbon-filament lamp. Others had made electric bulbs, but his long-lasting design and supply system made electric lighting practical.

events.title: Siege of Leningrad is lifted after 872 days
events.description: Soviet offensives drove German forces back from Leningrad, ending a blockade that began in September 1941. Some 800,000 or more civilians died, most from starvation.
events.html: Soviet offensives drove German forces back from Leningrad, ending a blockade that began in September 1941. Some 800,000 or more civilians died, most from starvation.

events.title: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
events.description: Red Army soldiers reached Auschwitz and found about 7,000 prisoners left behind. Around 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered there. The date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
events.html: Red Army soldiers reached Auschwitz and found about 7,000 prisoners left behind. Around 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered there. The date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

events.title: Fire kills three Apollo 1 astronauts during a test
events.description: A flash fire in the pure-oxygen cabin of Apollo 1 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee during a launch rehearsal at Cape Kennedy. NASA redesigned the spacecraft before flying again.
events.html: A flash fire in the pure-oxygen cabin of Apollo 1 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee during a launch rehearsal at Cape Kennedy. NASA redesigned the spacecraft before flying again.

events.title: Outer Space Treaty signed
events.description: The United States, the Soviet Union and Britain signed a treaty barring nuclear weapons from orbit and forbidding any nation from claiming the Moon or other celestial bodies. It remains the basis of space law.
events.html: The United States, the Soviet Union and Britain signed a treaty barring nuclear weapons from orbit and forbidding any nation from claiming the Moon or other celestial bodies. It remains the basis of space law.

intl.name: International Holocaust Remembrance Day
intl.description: Designated by the United Nations in 2005 to coincide with the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau, this day honours the memory of the six million Jewish victims and millions of others murdered by the Nazi regime.
